description: Region strings: what relay.onosendai.tech/<hex> and www.onosendai.tech/C/<hex> name, so a speakeasy URL and an ONOSENDAI link agree on the region (speakeasy ruling D7, 2026-11-04). Written from ONOSENDAI's own route code; this file is not normative. CYBERSPACE_V2.md defines the bit layout (section 2.2) and the hint box (section 7.7) but no region string; where a value here disagrees with that text, the text is right and the file is a bug.
format: input: the text after "/C/" in an ONOSENDAI path, or after "/" in a relay path, exactly as it appears in the URL (percent-encoding included).

Reading an input: percent-decode it once (decodeURIComponent; on a malformed escape keep the text undecoded); trim whitespace as JavaScript String.prototype.trim does; drop every trailing "/"; drop one leading "0x" or "0X"; lowercase. The result must be 1 to 64 hex characters, or the input is invalid (valid: false, and nothing else is given).
hex: the result. kind: "prefix" for 1 to 63 characters, "full" for 64.

A prefix of n characters fixes the top 4n bits of the coordinate (CYBERSPACE_V2.md section 2.2: x84 y84 z84 x83 ... z0, then the plane bit), so it names the aligned box of every coordinate whose 64-hex form starts with hex. Each axis keeps its own number of free low bits, its height; the heights are equal (a cube) only when n is a multiple of 3. The plane bit is the coordinate's lowest bit, so a prefix never fixes it: plane is null, and the box is the same in both planes.
A full coordinate is one gibson (every height 0) in the plane its lowest bit names.

region: per axis, min and max (inclusive) as decimal integers, height, and size = 2^height = max - min + 1; plane is 0, 1, or null for either plane. A coordinate is inside exactly when its 64-hex form starts with hex: each axis in [min, max], and, when plane is not null, the same plane.

inside and outside: coordinates as 64 lowercase hex characters with their axes as decimal integers and their plane, each one inside or outside the region. outside always holds one gibson past each face of the box where the space continues, and the box corner with the lowest and with the highest fixed bit flipped; for a full coordinate, also the same gibson in the other plane.

provenance.onosendai_code: src/lib/coordRoute.ts: parseCoordRoute, prefixRegion, coordPlace, placeHex; cyberspace-core coordToXyz

vectors.note: One character, the shortest prefix: the low corner of the whole space. Fixes x84 y84 z84 x83.

vectors.name: shortest-f
vectors.note: One character: x84 y84 z84 x83 all 1.

vectors.name: one-char-8
vectors.note: One character: only x84 is 1.

vectors.name: two-chars
vectors.note: Two characters, 8 bits fixed.

vectors.name: odd-length-3
vectors.note: An odd length: 12 bits fixed, 4 per axis.

vectors.name: odd-length-5
vectors.note: An odd length: 20 bits fixed.

vectors.name: cube-21
vectors.note: 21 characters fix 84 bits, 28 per axis: equal heights, a cube.

vectors.name: longest-62
vectors.note: 62 characters: 248 bits fixed.

vectors.note: 63 characters, the longest prefix: one bit free per axis and the plane bit open.

vectors.note: 64 characters: one gibson, the plane fixed by the last bit (1, ideaspace).

vectors.name: full-plane-0
vectors.note: 64 characters: one gibson, plane 0 (dataspace).

vectors.note: The origin of dataspace.

vectors.name: full-all-f
vectors.note: The far corner of ideaspace.

vectors.name: mixed-case

vectors.name: full-upper-case
vectors.note: 64 characters in upper case.

vectors.name: 0X-prefix
vectors.note: A leading 0X is dropped too.

vectors.name: full-0x-prefix

vectors.note: Trailing slashes are dropped.

vectors.note: Every trailing slash is dropped.

vectors.name: percent-encoded
vectors.note: The path is percent-decoded once, then read: abc.

vectors.name: encoded-slash
vectors.note: An encoded trailing slash decodes to a slash, which is then dropped.

vectors.note: Whitespace around the decoded text is trimmed (JavaScript String.prototype.trim).

vectors.note: U+00A0 is whitespace to trim.

vectors.name: encoded-bom
vectors.note: U+FEFF is whitespace to trim (JavaScript trim strips it; Go unicode.IsSpace does not).

vectors.name: zero-prefix-00
vectors.note: Leading zeros are significant: 00 is not 0.

vectors.name: invalid-not-hex

vectors.name: invalid-sign

vectors.name: invalid-nel
vectors.note: U+0085 is not whitespace to JavaScript trim (Go unicode.IsSpace says it is).
